title: Architecture assessment record (draft 0.1.0)
description: The record of one assessment of one version of a design: what was assessed, at what depth, against which lenses, by whom, what was found, where each finding went on the continuum, and the verdict. A finding names the criterion it answers, so a record can be compared with the next assessment of the same design. Draft: see standards/assessment/standard-architecture-assessment.md.

allOf.description: A production entry assessment is a review or deeper, except at triage tier AT1, where the team runs the production lens's tool criteria and the owner approves.

id.description: AS-NNN. Proposed by this draft and not yet in the envelope.

digest.description: The digest of the design specification assessed, so a finding cannot be read against a later version by mistake.

trigger.description: production-entry: the formal assessment of a solution as built, before it goes into production (standard, section 8.1). It brings in the production lens, and the record then needs an approval and an as-built conformance level.

stage_gate.description: The definition stage the assessment gates, when it gates one.

triage.description: The triage that chose this assessment (standard-assessment-triage.md): its record, the assessment type and the risk tier.

derived_tier.description: The tier the check derived from the specification. When it is higher than tier, the assessment stops and resumes at the derived tier.

depth.description: check: the automatic criteria only, run against the specification. review: every applicable criterion, automatic and reviewer. evaluation: a review plus scenario-based analysis with stakeholders (utility tree, sensitivity and trade-off points).

independent.description: Not an author of the design and not accountable for its delivery.

governance.description: How the review was governed. gate: an independent assessor and an approver. advice-process, at AT1 or AT2 only: the decider sought advice from those the design affects and from those with the expertise, recorded it as findings, and is accountable for the decision.

metrics.description: Optional measures of the practice itself.

days_to_verdict.description: From the request to the proposed outcome.

recurring_findings.description: Criteria failed again from an earlier assessment of the same subject.

incidents_traced.description: Incidents since the last assessment traced to a finding, or to a criterion that should have caught them.

utility_tree.description: Evaluation depth only: the scenarios the stakeholders prioritised, by quality attribute, with the design's own scenario ids where they exist.

criterion.description: The lens criterion the finding answers, for example CORE-QA-01.

result.description: The overall result. For a criterion decided by both, the reviewer's judgement, never better than tool_result.

tool_result.description: For a criterion decided by both: what the tool half found, whether the answer is present.

type.description: gap: the design does not say what it must. risk and non-risk, sensitivity and trade-off points: as ATAM defines them. observation: worth recording, not a defect.

evidence.description: The design paths, evidence ids or documents the finding rests on.

action.description: Where the finding goes on the continuum: a change to the design, a consideration (CN), a decision record (DR), a technical debt item (TD), a risk accepted by its owner, or a hand-over to another assessment (security, privacy, regulatory).

ref.description: The CN, DR, TD or hand-over reference, once it exists.

threatens.description: The design's goals or the outcomes (OC-NNN) the theme puts at risk.

approval.description: Production entry only: the accountable owner's decision on the verdict. A person, never an agent.

handovers.description: What this assessment does not decide and passes to an assessment that does: a cybersecurity assessment, a privacy impact assessment, an AI impact assessment, a regulatory conformity assessment.

conformance.description: TOGAF's levels of conformance (figure 6-1, as corrected by Technical Corrigendum 1), judged against the target state: the target architecture the catalogue records and the standards that govern it. How far the design's features and the target's requirements coincide, and whether what they share is in accordance.

as_built.description: Production entry only: the same TOGAF levels, applied to the built solution against this version of the design, which is the comparison TOGAF's compliance review makes.
